name: jlMPFRApply
doc: jlMPFRApply(func, x) applies the function pointer func to x. It is expected that the C function modifies the first parameters for the returned value (provided by FriCAS and returned here) and and as a last parameter, the rounding mode. See MPFR. Uses Julia rounding mode, default to nearest. \example{mpfr:=jlDlOpen "libmpfr"} \example{sym:= jlDlSym(mpfr,jsym(mpfr_gamma))} \example{val:=jfloat("0.7");} \example{jlMPFRApply(sym,val)} => 1.29805533264755778568117117915281161778... \example{jlDlClose(mpfr)}

Uses Julia rounding mode, default to nearest. \example{mpfr:=j lDlOpen "libmpfr"} \example{sym:= jlDlSym(mpfr,jsym(mpfr_pow))} \example{val:=jfloat("0.7");} \example{jlMPFRApply(sym,val, jfloat(2))} \example{jlDlClose(mpfr)}

It is expected that the C function modifies the first parameters for the returned value (provided by FriCAS and returned here) and as a last parameter, the rounding mode (the default mode is used here). See MPFR. Uses Julia rounding mode, default to nearest. \example{mpfr:=j lDlOpen "libmpfr"} \example{sym:= jlDlSym(mpfr,jsym(mpfr_fma))} \example{val:=jfloat("0.7");} \example{jlMPFRApply(sym,val, jfloat(2), jfloat(5))} \example{jlDlClose(mpfr)}

name: JLInt64
doc: This domain allows the manipulation of Julia Int64. Beware of internal Lisp implementations of machine integer, usually they differ, for example Lisp MOST-POSITIVE-FIXNUM on x86_64 GNU/Linux is 4611686018427387903 with SBCL whereas it is 11 52921504606846975 with Clozure CL. They will be passed as an Int64 to Julia nevertheless, but returned value can possibl y not fit in a Lisp fixnum. In Julia, typemax(Int64) is 9223372036854775807 on this arch. This domain is therefore not i ntended to perform "advanced" computation, it just includes basic arithmetic and is used, for example, for returned pivo t vectors in linear algebra.

name: JLFloat32
doc: JLFloat32 implements 32 bits floating point arithmetic using Julia Float32 type. Bear in mind that, like JLInt64, the in ternal representation depends on the underlying Lisp implementation, so the usual pure arithmetic operations occur there . For example: \example{libm:= jlDlOpen "libopenlibm"} \example{squareRoot:= jlDlSym(libm,jsym(sqrt))} \example{jlDlCApply(squareRoot, "Cdouble", jobject("2."), "Cdouble")} \example{sinus:=jlDlSym(libm,jsym(sin))} \example{jlDlCApply(sinus,"Float64", jobject("2."), "Float64")}

name: jlDlCApply

name: jlDlCApply

name: jlDlOpen
doc: jlDlOpen(lib) opens/loads the dynamic shared library lib and returns a reference pointer that can be used to obtain addresses of its exported symbols using jlDlSym. It is up to the user to unload the shared object when it is no longer used. Does not throw an error if the library cannot be loaded and returns 'nothing' in this case. Use the nothing? operation on the returned value if necessary.

name: jlDlOpen
doc: jlDlOpen(lib, flags) opens/loads the dynamic shared library lib and returns a reference pointer that can be used to obtain addresses of its exported symbols using jlDlSym. It is up to the user to unload the shared object when it is no longer used. Does not throw an error if the library cannot be loaded by default and returns nothing in this case. Use the nothing? operation on the returned value if necessary. The Julia module Libdl must be loaded/imported before using this function. \example{jlUsing "Libdl"} -- for flags \example{jlDlOpen("libopenlibm", jobject "Libdl.RTLD_NOW")} flags can be one or combination of: RTLD_DEEPBIND RTLD_FIRST RTLD_GLOBAL RTLD_LAZY RTLD_LOCAL RTLD_NODELETE RTLD_NOLOAD RTLD_NOW Note: the Julia module Libdl must be loaded or imported before using these flags.

name: jlDlOpen

It is up to the user to unload the shared object when it is no longer used. 'throw' determines whether or not Julia throws an error if the library cannot be loaded. \example{jlDlOpen("libopenlibm", true)}

name: jlDlOpen
doc: jlDlOpen(lib, flags, throw) opens/loads the dynamic shared library lib and returns a reference pointer that can be used to obtain addresses of its exported symbols using jlDlSym. It is up to the user to unload the shared object when it is no longer used. Does not throw an error if the library cannot be loaded by default and returns nothing in this case. Use the nothing? operation on the returned value if necessary. 'throw' determines whether or not Julia throws an error if the library cannot be loaded. The Julia module must be be loaded/imported before using this function. \example{jlDlOpen("libopenlibm", jobject "Libdl.RTLD_NOW", false)} flags can be one or combination of: RTLD_DEEPBIND RTLD_FIRST RTLD_GLOBAL RTLD_LAZY RTLD_LOCAL RTLD_NODELETE RTLD_NOLOAD RTLD_NOW Note: the Julia module Libdl must be loaded or imported before using these flags.

name: jlDlClose

For example, global optimization from the SIAM 100 digits challenge: \example{x := jWSExpr(x);y:=jWSExpr y;} \example{expr := exp(sin(50*x))+sin(60*exp(y))+ sin(70*sin(x))+ sin(sin(80*y))-sin(10*(x+y))+(x^2+y^2)/4} \example{numericMinimize(expr, jWSList [x,y])}

doc: dSolveValue(expr,funcs, vars) returns the value determined by the differential equation(s) in expr for the function(s) funcs with independent variable(s) vars. \example{x:=jWSExpr x;} \example{f:=derivative(operator('f),0)} \example{f0:=derivative(operator('f),0,0)} \example{fx:=derivative(operator('f),0,x)} \example{fprimex:=derivative(operator('f),1,x)} \example{dSolveValue(jWSExpr([jWSEqual(fprimex + fx , a *sin(x)/cos(x)), jWSEqual(f0,0)]),f,x)}

name: dSolveValue
doc: dSolveValue(eq, func,var) returns the value determined by the differential equation eq for the function func with independent variable var.

name: numericDSolve
doc: numericDSolve(expr,fun,xrange) solves numerically the differential equation(s) in expr for the function fun, in the range xrange. Other combinations of parameters are also available.

name: numericDSolve
doc: numericDSolve(eq,fun,xrange) solves numerically the differential equation eq for the function fun, in the range xrange.

name: numericDSolve
doc: numericDSolve(expr,fun,xrange,yrange) solves numerically the differential equation(s) in expr for the function fun, in the ranges xrange and yrange. Other combinations of parameters are also available (see documentation).

name: numericDSolveValue
doc: numericDSolveValue(expr,fun,xrange) returns the numerical value solution of the differential equation(s) in expr for the function fun, in the range xrange. Other combinations of parameters are also available (see documentation).

name: numericDSolveValue
doc: numericDSolveValue(eq,fun,xrange) returns the numerical solution of the differential equation eq for the function fun, in the range xrange.

name: numericDSolveValue
doc: numericDSolveValue(expr,fun,xrange,yrange) returns the numerical solution of the differential equation(s) in expr for the function fun, in the ranges xrange and yrange. Other combinations of parameters are also available (see documentation).

name: residue
doc: residue(expr, {x,x0}) returns the residue of expr at x0.

name: residueSum
doc: residueSum(expr, var) returns the residue of expr. \example{residueSum(Gamma(x),x)}

name: reduce
doc: reduce(expr,lvars) tries to reduce the equation in expr.

name: reduce
doc: reduce(expr,lvars) tries to reduce the (in)equation in expr.

name: reduce
doc: reduce(expr,lvars,dom) tries to reduce the equation in expr.

name: reduce
doc: reduce(expr,lvars,dom) tries to reduce the (in)equation in expr.

name: findInstance
doc: findInstance(expr,lvars) tries to find an instance of the equation in expr.

name: findInstance
doc: findInstance(expr,lvars) tries to find an instance of the (in)equation in expr.

name: findInstance
doc: findInstance(expr,lvars,dom) tries to find an instance of the equation in expr.

name: findInstance
doc: findInstance(expr,lvars,dom,n) tries to find n instance(s) to the equation in expr.

name: findInstance
doc: findInstance(expr,lvars,dom) tries to find an instance to the equation in expr.

name: findInstance
doc: findInstance(expr,lvars,dom, n) tries to find n instance(s) to the (in)equation in expr.

name: numerator
doc: numerator(expr) returns the numerator of expr.

name: denominator
doc: denominator(expr) returns the denominator of expr.

name: numerDenom
doc: numerDenom(expr) returns the numerator and denominator of expr.

name: polynomial?
doc: polynomial?(p,x) checks whether or not p is a polynomial in x.

name: polynomial?
doc: polynomial?(p,vlist) checks whether or not p is a polynomial in the list of variables vlist.

name: polynomialExpression?
doc: polynomialExpression?(p,x) checks whether or not p is a polynomial expression in x.

name: polynomialExpression?
doc: polynomialExpression?(p,vlist) checks whether or not p is a polynomial expression in the list of variables vlist.

name: rationalExpression?
doc: rationalExpression?(p,x) checks whether or not p is a rational expression in x.

name: rationalExpression?
doc: rationalExpression?(p,vlist) checks whether or not p is a rational expression in the list of variables vlist.

name: variables
doc: variables(p) returns the list of variables in p.

name: exponent
doc: exponent(p,expr) returns the maximum exponent of p for expr. \example{x:= jWSExpr x;y := jWSExpr y} \example{p:=(x^2-2)^3*(y*x^3+x^11*y^7)*(y^5+x*y^2+x^11+y)} \example{exponent(%,(x^2-2))}

name: exponent
doc: exponent(p, expr, map) applies map to the exponents related to expr and returns it. By default map = "Max". \example{x:= jWSExpr x;y := jWSExpr y} \example{p:=expand((x^2-2)^3*(y*x^3+x^11*y^7)*(y^5+x*y^2+x^11+y))} \example{exponent(p,x,"Min")}

name: coefficient
doc: coefficient(p,expr) returns the coefficient of expr in p. \example{x:= jWSExpr x} \example{coefficient((x - y)^4, x * y^3)}

name: coefficient
doc: coefficient(p, expr, n) returns the coefficient of expr^n in p.

name: coefficientList
doc: coefficientList(p,expr) returns the list of coefficients of expr in p.

name: coefficientRules
doc: coefficientRules(p) returns the coefficients and exponents of p as WS rules.

name: coefficientRules
doc: coefficientRules(p,vars) returns the coefficients and exponents of p with respect to var(s) as WS rules.

name: fromCoefficientRules
doc: fromCoefficientRules(list, vars) constructs the polynomial from the list of coefficients and exponents rules. \example{x:= jWSExpr x;y := jWSExpr y} \example{coefficientRules((x + y)^2+x^11,jWSExpr [x,y])} \example{fromCoefficientRules(%, jWSExpr [x,y])}

name: monomialList
doc: monomialList(p) returns the list of monomials in p.

name: polynomialQuotient
doc: polynomialQuotient(p1, p2, x) returns the quotient of p1 and p2 in x.

name: polynomialRemainder
doc: polynomialRemainder(p1,p2, x) returns the remainder of p1 and p2 in x.

name: polynomialQuotientRemainder
doc: polynomialQuotientRemainder(p1,p2,var) returns the quotient and remainder of p1 and p2 in x.

name: padeApproximant
doc: padeApproximant(expr, "{x,x0, {n,m}"}) returns the Padé approximant at x0.

name: symmetricPolynomial
doc: symmetricPolynomial(n,lvars) returns the n-th elementary symmetric polynomial with respect to variables in lvars.

name: symmetricReduction
doc: symmetricReduction(f,lvars) returns a pair of polynomials representing f = p+q where p is a symmetric polynomial, q the remainder.

name: symmetricReduction
doc: symmetricReduction(f, lvars, replnt) returns a pair of polynomials representing f = p+q where p is a symmetric polynomial, q the remainder where variables in p replaced by the ones in replnt.

name: polynomialGCD
doc: polynomialGCD(p1, p2) returns the greatest common divisor of p1 and p2.

name: polynomialGCD
doc: polynomialGCD(p1, p2, opt) returns the greatest common divisor of p1 and p2 with options opt, for example Modulus->p.

name: polynomialExtendedGCD
doc: polynomialExtendedGCD(p1, p2, x) returns the greatest common divisor of p1 and p2 considered as univariate polynomials in x

name: polynomialLCM
doc: polynomialLCM(p1,p2) returns the least common divisor of p1 and p2.

name: polynomialLCM
doc: polynomialLCM(p1,p2,opt) returns the least common divisor of p1 and p2 with options opt, for example an Extension rule.

name: polynomialMod
doc: polynomialMod(p,mod) reduces modulo p the integer coefficients of the polynomial p.

name: resultant
doc: resultant(p1,p2,x) returns the resultant of p1 and p2.

name: subResultants
doc: subResultants(p1,p2,x) returns the subresultant of p1 and p2 with respect to x.

name: discriminant
doc: discriminant(p, x) returns the discriminant of p with respect to x.

name: groebnerBasis
doc: groebnerBasis(lpoly, lvar) computes a Groebner basis from the list of polynomials lpoly relative to the list of vars lvars.

name: groebnerBasis
doc: groebnerBasis(lpoly, lvar, opt) computes a Groebner basis from the list of polynomials lpoly relative to the list of variables in lvars without variables in opt. Opt can also give the modulus to compute it: "Modulus -> p".

name: polynomialReduce
doc: polynomialReduce(poly,lpoly,lvar) returns a minimal representation of the polynomial poly in terms of the polynomial list lpoly with respect to the list of variables lvar.

name: factorPolynomial
doc: factorPolynomial(p) factorizes the polynomial p. For example: \example{x := jWSExpr x} \example{p:=expand(chebyshevT(7,x)* chebyshevU(9,x))} \example{factorPolynomial p}

name: factor
doc: factor(expr) factors the expression or polynomial expr.

name: factor
doc: factor(expr, opt) factors the expression or polynomial expr. For example: \example{x := jWSExpr x;} \example{factor(1 + x^2, "GaussianIntegers -> True")}

name: factorSquareFree
doc: factorSquareFree(expr) factors the expression or polynomial expr in square free factors.

name: factorTerms
doc: factorTerms(p) factors out numerical factors of the expression or polynomial expr.

name: factorTerms
doc: factorTerms(p, var) factors out numerical factors of the expression or polynomial expr without those related to var.

name: factorTerms
doc: factorTerms(p, vars) factors the expression or polynomial expr by pulling out numerical factors without those related to var(s).

name: factorTermsList
doc: factorTermsList(expr) is the counterpart of factorTerms but here returned as a list of pairs (numerical factor, polynomial factor).

name: factorTermsList
doc: factorTermsList(expr, vars) is the counterpart of factorTerms but here returned as a list of pairs (numerical factor, polynomial factor). The numerical factors related to var(s) are not factored.

name: factorList
doc: factorList(expr) factors the expression or polynomial expr, but returns the result as a list of pairs (factor, exponent).

name: factorSquareFreeList
doc: factorSquareFreeList(expr) factors the expression or polynomial expr in square free factors but returns the result as a list of pairs (factor, exponent).

name: irreducible?
doc: irreducible?(p) checks whether or not p is irreducible.

name: irreducible?
doc: irreducible?(p) checks whether or not p is irreducible over Gaussian rationals or algebraic extensions.

name: decompose
doc: decompose(poly, x) is a polynomial decomposition function, here, related to x.

name: interpolatingPolynomial
doc: interpolatingPolynomial(lpoly,x) interpolates the list of polynomials lpoly with respect to x.

name: minimalPolynomial
doc: minimalPolynomial(expr,var) returns the minimal polynomial in the variable var of the expression expr.

name: minimalPolynomial
doc: minimalPolynomial(expr,var, elem) returns the minimal polynomial in the variable var of the expression expr.

name: findRoot
doc: findRoot(expr,start) tries to find the root of expr starting at start. \example{x:= jWSExpr x} \example{findRoot(sin(x) + cos(x), "\{x, 0\}")}

name: normal
doc: normal(expr) converts expr to a normal expression from different expression types. Can be applied to a power series for example. For example: \example{x:=jWSExpr x} \example{s:=series(exp(x),jWSExpr "\{x,0,10\}")} \example{normal(s)::EXPR INT}

name: normal
doc: normal(expr, list(Head)||Head) converts objects in expr to a normal expression form from different expression types, with Head, or a list of Head-s.

name: simplify
doc: simplify(expr) simplifies the expr. \example{x:=jWSExpr("x"); simplify(sqrt(x^2)^2)}

name: simplify
doc: simplify(expr, assumptions) simplifies the expression expr assuming that assumptions are satisfied. For example: \example{x:=jWSExpr("x"); simplify(sqrt(x^2), "x>0")}

name: extendedSimplify
doc: extendedSimplify(expr) is the extended version of simplify. This is the full version of simplify. \example{x:= jWSExpr x} \example{expr := Gamma(x)/Gamma(x-1)} Compare with simplify(expr). \example{extendedSimplify(expr)}

name: extendedSimplify
doc: extendedSimplify(expr, assumptions) is the extended version of simplify with respect to assumptions or ExcludedForms. This is the full version.

name: refine
doc: refine(expr, assums) refines the expression expr with assumptions assums.

name: assuming
doc: assuming(assumption(s), expr) uses the assumptions for use of expr with refine, simplify and integrate for example. The assumption(s) are not always supported by MathLink. Use assumptions with 'refine' etc. directly instead.

name: expand
doc: expand(expr) puts out products and positive powers of integers of the expression expr.

name: expand
doc: expand(expr, opt) is the expand version with excluded pattern-s or any other options available (for example "Modulus->p").

name: extendedExpand
doc: extendedExpand(expr) puts out all products and positive powers of integers.

name: collect
doc: collect(expr, var) collects same power terms with respect to variable var.

name: collect
doc: collect(expr, vars) collects same power terms with respect to variables in vars.

name: apart
doc: apart(expr) converts a rational expression as a sum of terms, reducing denominator(s).

name: apart
doc: apart(expr, vars) converts a rational expression as a sum of terms as the one arg apart does but only for vars (the others are considered as constants).

name: expandNumerator
doc: expandNumerator(expr) expands numerators of rational expression expr.

name: expandDenominator
doc: expandDenominator(expr) expands denominators of rational expression expr.

name: cancel
doc: cancel(expr) cancels common factors in numerators and denominators of the rational expression expr.

name: together
doc: together(expr) puts together terms over a common denominator cancelling common factors.

name: distribute
doc: distribute(expr) distributes expr over addition. For illustration: \example{distribute(jWSExpr "(x + y) * (a + b + c)")}

name: distribute
doc: distribute(f,g) distributes f over g.

name: hornerForm
doc: hornerForm(expr, x) returns the Horner form of expr (minimizing multiplications).

name: powerExpand
doc: powerExpand(expr) expands powers in expr assuming no branch cut.

name: powerExpand
doc: powerExpand(expr, sym) expands powers in expr with respect to sym, assuming no branch cut.

name: complexExpand
doc: complexExpand(expr) expands expr assuming variables are real.

name: complexExpand
doc: complexExpand(expr, cvars) expands expr assuming all but cvars variables are real.

name: trigExpand
doc: trigExpand(expr) tries to expand (hyperbolic) trigonometric functions in expr.

name: functionExpand
doc: functionExpand(expr) tries to expand functions in expr to more elementary functions. For example: \example{functionExpand sphericalBesselJ(3,8)}

name: functionExpand
doc: functionExpand(expr,assumptions) tries to expand functions in expr to more elementary functions assuming that assumptions are satisfied.

name: trigReduce
doc: trigReduce(expr) reduces power and products of trigonometric functions.

name: rootReduce
doc: rootReduce(expr) reduces root functions.

name: trigFactor
doc: trigFactor(expr) factors (hyperbolic) trigonometric functions in expr.

name: trigFactorList
doc: trigFactorList(expr) returns a list of factors of (hyperbolic) trigonometric functions in expr.

name: trigToExp
doc: trigToExp(expr) returns expr with (hyperbolic) trigonometric functions converted to, eventually complex, exponentials.

name: expToTrig
doc: expToTrig(expr) returns expr with exponentials converted to (hyperbolic) trigonometric functions.

name: toString
doc: toString(expr, form) returns the string representation of expr with WS language format form.

name: toExpression
doc: toExpression(expr) converts expr to a WS expression and evaluates it.

name: toExpression
doc: toExpression(expr, form) converts expr to a WS expression and evaluates it with output in the format form.

name: toExpression
doc: toExpression(expr, form, h) converts expr to a WS expression and evaluates it with output in the format form but wrapping the head with h. `Hold` for example.

name: rationalApproximation
doc: rationalApproximation(expr) tries to find a rational approximation of the expression expr.

name: rationalApproximation
doc: rationalApproximation(expr, dx) tries to find a rational approximation of the expression expr within tolerance dx.

name: jlGreedyEval
doc: jlGreedyEval(bool) toggles automatic arithmetic operations. Plus[a, a] can become Times[2, a] using or not Julia `weval`.

name: jlEval
doc: jlEval(expr, param) evaluates expression expr with param as parameter(s). See also `eval` or `replaceAll`. For example: \example{x:=jWSExpr("x");jlEval(sqrt(x),"x=2.0")}

name: jlEval
doc: jlEval(expr, param1, param2) evaluates expression expr with param1 and param2 as parameters. See also `eval` or `replaceAll`. \example{a:=jWSExpr("a");b:=jWSExpr("b");} \example{jlEval(sqrt(a^2+b^2),"a=1.0","b=1.0")}

name: jlEval
doc: jlEval(expr, param11, param2, param3) evaluates expression expr with param1, param2 and param3 as parameters. See also `eval` or `replaceAll`.

name: length
doc: length(expr) returns the length of expr seen as a list.

name: level
doc: level(expr, lev) returns the list of expression expr at level lev.

name: level
doc: level(expr, lev, head) returns the list of expression expr at level lev with heads if head is true.

name: extract
doc: extract(expr,i) returns the i-th element of expr seen as a list.

name: keys
doc: keys(expr) returns the key elements in expr if any.

name: values
doc: values(expr) returns the values elements in expr.

name: lookup
doc: lookup(assocs,keys) returns value(s) associated to key(s).

name: lookup
doc: lookup(assocs,keys, defaultval) returns value(s) associated to key(s) if key(s) exist(s), otherwise defaultval

name: quantityUnit
doc: quantityUnit(val) returns unit of val.

name: quantityMagnitude
doc: quantityMagnitude(val) returns magnitude of val.

name: jlDisplay
doc: jlDisplay(expr) returns the traditional form of expr. This is equivalent to: jWSExpr "Format[Sin[x]]" => sin(x)

name: jlDisplay
doc: jlDisplay(expr, form) returns the `form` form of expr resulting for example in: "Format[Sin[x], TeXForm]" => \sin x

name: baseForm
doc: baseForm(x, n) returns the printed representation of x in base b.

name: numberForm
doc: numberForm(x) returns the default printed representation of x.

name: numberForm
doc: numberForm(x, expr) returns the approximate printed representation of x with expr as specification (number of digits of precision or a 2-list of number of digits and the number of digits after the decimal point).

name: decimalForm
doc: decimalForm(x) returns the printed representation of x in decimal form i.e. without scientific notation.

name: decimalForm
doc: decimalForm(x, expr) returns the printed representation of x in decimal form with expr as specification (number of digits of precision or a 2-list of number of digits and the number of digits after the decimal point).

name: scientificForm
doc: scientificForm(x) returns the printed representation of x in scientific form.

name: scientificForm
doc: scientificForm(x,n) returns the printed representation of x in scientific form with n digits of precision.

name: engineeringForm
doc: engineeringForm(x) returns the printed representation of x in engineering form.

name: engineeringForm
doc: engineeringForm(x,n) returns the printed representation of x in engineering form with n digits of precision.

name: percentForm
doc: percentForm(x) returns the printed representation of x in percent form. For example: \example{percentForm jWSExpr 0.50}

name: percentForm
doc: percentForm(x,n) returns the printed representation of x in percent with n digits of precision.

name: accountingForm
doc: accountingForm(x,n) returns the accounting printed representation of x.

name: accountingForm
doc: accountingForm(x,n) returns the accounting printed representation of x with n digits of precision.

name: matrixForm
doc: matrixForm(mat) returns a pretty-printable form of mat i.e. its WS 'MatrixForm'.

name: traditionalForm
doc: traditionalForm(expr) returns a traditional form of expr i.e. its WS 'TraditionalForm'.

name: quantityForm
doc: quantityForm(expr,form) returns expr as a quantity with format form.

name: quantityForm
doc: quantityForm(expr,lform) returns expr as a quantity with a list of formats lform.

name: replace
doc: replace(expr, rule) applies rule(s) to expr.

name: replace
doc: replace(expr, rule, lev) applies rule to expr with level lev.

name: replacePart
doc: replacePart(expr, part) replaces expr using rule(s) expressing position(s).

name: replaceAt
doc: replaceAt(expr, part, n) replaces the n-th element of expr using rule(s).

name: replaceAll
doc: replaceAll(expr, rule) applies rule(s) to expr.

name: replaceRepeated
doc: replaceRepeated(expr, rule) applies rule(s) to expr, but repeatedly.

name: select
doc: select(expr, form) selects elements of expr if form(element) is true.

name: select
doc: select(expr, form, n) selects the n first elements of expr if form(element) is true.

name: retractIfCan
doc: retractIfCan(expr) retracts expr to a JLFloat64 if it can be retracted to a 64 bits machine float.

name: retractIfCan
doc: retractIfCan(expr) retracts expr to a DoubleFloat if it can be retracted to a Lisp machine float.

name: retractIfCan
doc: retractIfCan(expr) tries to retract expr to an Expression(Integer).

name: retractIfCan
doc: retractIfCan(expr) tries to retract expr to an Expression(Float).

name: retract
doc: retract(expr) tries to retract expr to an Expression(Integer). Throws an error otherwise.

name: retract
doc: retract(expr) tries to retract expr to an Expression(Integer). Throws an error otherwise.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(z) coerces the integer z to a WSExpression. Convenience function.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(gi) coerces gi to a WSExpression. Convenience function.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(q) coerces the rational q to a WSExpression. Convenience function.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(f) coerces the floating point number f to a WSExpression. Convenience function.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(eq) coerces the equation eq to a WSExpression equation.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(str) coerces the string str to a WSExpression evaluating str as a Wolfram Symbolic Language Expression. For example: \example{expr := "Sqrt[x]"::WSEXPR;jlEval(expr,"x=2.0")}

name: coerce
doc: coerce(sym) coerces sym to a WSExpression.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(sym) coerces sym to a WSExpression.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(list) coerces list of WSExpression.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(expr) coerces expr to a WSInteger if possible.

name: coerce
doc: coerce(expr) coerces expr to a WSRational if possible.

name: jlWSPrecision
doc: jlWSPrecision get precision of expr.

name: jlWSAccuracy
doc: jlWSAccuracy(expr) get accuracy of expr.

name: jlWSSetPrecision
doc: jlWSSetPrecision(expr, prec) sets precision of expr to prec.

name: jlWSSetAccuracy
doc: jlWSSetAccuracy(expr, acc) sets accuracy of expr to acc.

name: jlWSSetOptions
doc: jlWSSetOptions(type, opts) sets some internal engine options.

name: jWSData
doc: jWSData() returns the list of WS symbols. Note: Currently unprintable.

name: jWSData
doc: jWSData(sym) returns the entity(ies) associated to sym(s).

name: jWSData
doc: jWSData(sym, prop) returns the property of sym.

name: jWSData
doc: jWSData(sym, prop, ann) returns the annotation for the property of sym.

name: jWSData
doc: jWSData(sym) returns the entity(ies) associated to sym(s).

name: jWSData
doc: jWSData(sym, prop) returns the property of sym.

name: jWSData
doc: jWSData(sym, prop, ann) returns the annotation for the property of sym.

name: jWSAssociation
doc: jWSAssociation(rules) returns the associations (key->value) created from the rules.

name: jWSTable
doc: jWSTable(expr, range) applies the expr to the defined range.

name: jWSTable
doc: jWSTable(expr, range1, range2) applies the expr to the defined ranges.

name: jWSRule
doc: jWSRule(lhs,rhs) returns the Julia WS rule lhs->rhs.

name: jWSRule
doc: jWSRule(eq) returns the Julia WS rule lhs->rhs for the equation eq. For example: \example{x := jWSExpr x} \example{p := 1/2 * legendreQ(5,x)} \example{replaceAll(p, jWSRule(x = jWSExpr "1.55555556444883838383833777333333333"))}

name: jWSEqual
doc: jWSEqual(lhs,rhs) returns the Julia WS equality lhs == rhs.

name: jWSNotEqual
doc: jWSNotEqual(lhs,rhs) returns the Julia WS inequality lhs != rhs.

name: jWSLess
doc: jWSLess(lhs,rhs) returns the Julia WS inequality lhs < rhs.

name: jWSLessEqual
doc: jWSLessEqual(lhs,rhs) returns the Julia WS inequality lhs <= rhs.

name: jWSGreater
doc: jWSGreater(lhs,rhs) returns the Julia WS inequality lhs > rhs.

name: jWSGreaterEqual
doc: jWSGreaterEqual(lhs,rhs) returns the Julia WS inequality lhs >= rhs.

name: jWSQuantity
doc: jWSQuantity(jWSString(u)) returns quantity unit u of 1. For example: \example{jWSQuantity jWSString "Meter"}

name: jWSQuantity
doc: jWSQuantity(x,jWSString(u)) returns quantity unit u of x. For example: \example{jWSQuantity(1.2, jWSString "Meter")}

name: jWSExpr
doc: jWSExpr(sym) coerces sym to a WSExpression. For example: x := jWSExpr x

name: jWSExpr
doc: jWSExpr(z) returns the Integer z as a WSExpression.

name: jWSExpr
doc: jWSExpr(q) returns the Fraction(Integer) q as a WSExpression.

name: jWSExpr
doc: jWSExpr(r) returns the DoubleFloat as a WSExpression.

name: jWSExpr
doc: jWSExpr(r) returns the JLFloat64 as a WSExpression.

name: jWSExpr
doc: jWSExpr(r) returns the Float r as a WSExpression.

name: jWSExpr
doc: jWSExpr(r) returns the JLFloat r as a WSExpression.

name: jWSExpr
doc: jWSExpr(list) returns the list of WSExpression as a WSExpression.

name: jWSExpr
doc: jWSExpr(str) constructs str as a WSExpression evaluating str as a Wolfram Symbolic Language expression. For example: \example{jWSExpr "Factorial[5]"} \example{jWSExpr "3.14159"} \example{jlWSDateString(jWSExpr "Tomorrow")} \example{toString jWSExpr "TextSentences[WikipediaData[_"Sun_"]][[;; 40]]"} Example: jWSExpr "Probability[x < 1, x \[Distributed] NormalDistribution[]]"

name: WSNumericalSpecialFunctions
doc: Julia Wolfram Symbolic numerical special functions using the MathLink Julia package.

name: sign
doc: sign(x) is 1 if x is positive, -1 if x is negative, 0 if x equals 0.

name: Gamma
doc: Gamma(z) is the Euler Gamma function.

name: Gamma
doc: Gamma(a, z) is the incomplete Gamma function.

name: Gamma
doc: Gamma(a,z1,z2) computes the generalized incomplete Gamma function.

name: Beta
doc: Beta(x, y) is \spad{Gamma(x) * Gamma(y)/Gamma(x+y)}.

name: Beta
doc: Beta(z, a, b) is the incomplete Beta function.

name: digamma
doc: digamma(z) is the logarithmic derivative of \spad{Gamma(z)} (often written \spad{psi(z)} in the literature).

name: digamma
doc: digamma(n,z) is the n-th derivative of the digamma function.

name: polygamma
doc: polygamma(k, z) is the \spad{k-th} derivative of \spad{digamma(z)}, (often written \spad{psi(k, z)} in the literature).

name: besselJ
doc: besselJ(v, z) is the Bessel function of the first kind.

name: besselJZero
doc: besselJZero(n,x) returns the n-th zero of the Bessel J n-th function.

name: besselY

name: jlWSImport
doc: jlWSImport(src) imports the source src. For example: \example{file:=jlWSImport jWSString "examples/customers-100.csv";} \example{jlWSDateString(file.2.11)}

name: jlWSImport
doc: jlWSImport(myfile, form) imports the file myfile with format form. For example: \example{file:=jlWSImport(jWSString("examples/customers-100.csv"), jWSString "CSV");}

name: jlWSFileFormat
doc: jlWSFileFormat(src) tries to determine the format of the source src from its content. Can be used with jWSImport. For example: \example{jlWSFileFormat("examples/customers-100.csv")}

name: jlWSFileFormat
doc: jlWSFileFormat(src, list(form)) tries to determine the format of the source src from its content using the list of formats form. Returns WS None if no format is found. Can be used with jWSImport. For example: \spad{jlWSFileFormat("examples/customers-100.csv",jWSExpr "{_"CSV_",_"TSV_"}")}

name: jlWSSnippet

name: jlWSExport
doc: jlWSExport(file.ext, obj) exports the object obj to the file file.ext. The extension ext will determine the saved format. A WS expression for example can be exported in an image file, it will be saved in the WS 'StandardForm' whereas in FriCAS it is displayed in WS 'OutputForm': \example{x:=jWSExpr(x);jlWSExport("legendreP.png", legendreP(7, x))}

name: jlWSExportString
doc: jlWSExportString(expr, form) returns the string representation of expr in the specified format. Use toString or string to obtain the FriCAS String. For example: \example{jWSExpr \"Probability[x < 0, x \\[Distributed] NormalDistribution[]]\"} \example{jWSExpr \"Probability[x < 1, x \\[Distributed] NormalDistribution[]]\"} \example{string jlWSExportString(%,jWSString "TeX")}

name: jlWSPlot
doc: jlWSPlot(expr, options) is the WS plot function. Since it should be run in a Wolfram notebook or any other supported graphical interfaces, the Wolfram Jupyter "plugin" for example, it is left to the user for testing purposes. The following uses the jlWSExport function: \example{x:=jWSExpr(x);opt:=jWSList [x,-5,5]} \example{jlWSExport("sin.png", jlWSPlot(sin(x),opt))}

name: jlWSSeedRandom!
